concepts.title: Sole Proprietorship: Features, Merits and Limitations
concepts.definition: Sole proprietorship is a form of business owned, managed and controlled by a single individual who bears all risks, takes all profits, and has unlimited liability with no separate legal existence.
concepts.key_idea: Formation and closure are easy, secrecy is complete, and direct incentive plus quick decision making make it suitable for small scale ventures.

solution_steps.explain: Confirm one person owns, manages and controls the business.
Verify unlimited liability and absence of separate legal existence.

concepts.title: Partnership: Deed, Registration, Liability and Types of Partners
concepts.definition: Partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all, governed by a partnership deed and the Partnership Act, with unlimited joint and several liability of partners.
concepts.key_idea: Registration is optional, and partners may be active, sleeping, secret, minor or nominal partners, with the partnership deed covering profit sharing ratio, capital, duties and dispute settlement.

solution_steps.explain: Confirm the profit sharing agreement among partners.

concepts.title: Cooperative Society and Joint Stock Company
concepts.definition: A cooperative society is a voluntary association for mutual welfare with one member one vote and service motive, while a joint stock company is an artificial person with separate legal entity, perpetual succession, common seal, limited liability and transferable shares.
concepts.key_idea: The company form suits large capital needs and professional management, while cooperatives protect members from middlemen through service rather than profit motive.

concepts.title: Choice of Form of Business Organisation
concepts.definition: The choice among sole proprietorship, partnership, cooperative society and company depends on cost and ease of formation, liability, capital requirement, continuity, control, management ability and nature of business.
concepts.key_idea: Small ventures with limited capital suit proprietorship, growing firms take the partnership route, and large scale enterprises needing heavy investment adopt the company form.
